intro:
AI phone answering for a restaurant can cost a little or a lot, depending on the pricing model. The simplest answer is that ROAL charges **$0.90 per completed phone order**, with no monthly fee, setup fee, per-minute fee, or contract.

That matters because many other phone options charge you even when the phone is quiet. You can compare that against [monthly AI phone plans](/compare/monthly-ai-phone-plans) and your own phone volume.

sections.h2: What does AI phone answering usually cost a restaurant?
sections.body:
Most restaurant owners see three pricing styles: per order, monthly, or per minute/call. For AI phone tools, many charge a fixed monthly fee per location, often roughly $79 to $599, whether or not orders come in. Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call, which can be hard to predict on a busy weekend.

ROAL uses a simple per-order model: **$0.90 per completed phone order**. A completed order means the caller confirms the order and the ticket reaches the kitchen screen. Calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free. That makes it easier to match cost to revenue.

Here is a quick owner check:
- If the phone rings a lot but only a few calls become orders, per-order pricing can be easier to live with.
- If you want flat monthly spending, a monthly plan may feel simpler.
- If you already pay staff to answer the phone, compare the total with [phone staff cost](/tools/phone-staff-cost-calculator).

sections.h2: How do I compare per-order pricing with monthly plans?
sections.body:
Use your own numbers. Say your average phone order is **$28**. If an AI phone host charges **$0.90 per completed order**, that is about **3.2% of that order**. If your average order is **$42**, the same $0.90 is about **2.1%**. Plug in your own average ticket and order count to see the real cost for your shop.

Now compare that with a monthly plan. Say a monthly tool costs **$199** and you only get 80 completed phone orders in a month. Your cost per completed order is about **$2.49** before you count any other charges. If you get 300 completed orders, the monthly plan becomes about **66 cents** per completed order.

A simple way to compare:
1. Write down your monthly completed phone orders.
2. Multiply by $0.90 for ROAL.
3. Compare that number with the monthly fee from other phone tools.
4. Add any setup fee, contract risk, or extra call charges.

For a deeper look, see [per-minute vs per-order pricing](/blog/per-minute-vs-per-order-pricing).

sections.h2: What hidden costs should I watch for?
sections.body:
Price per month is not the whole story. Restaurant owners often get surprised by setup fees, per-minute billing, overage charges, or contracts that keep costs locked in even when business slows down. Some tools also charge extra for more locations, more call volume, or additional features that should really be standard.

With ROAL, the pricing is straightforward: **no monthly fee, no setup fee, no per-minute fee, and no contract**. ROAL also says calls, questions, and test calls are unlimited and free, and billing is monthly. That makes it easier to forecast your bill from actual completed orders.

Use this checklist before you sign anything:
- Ask what counts as a billable order.
- Ask whether questions and test calls cost money.
- Ask whether there is a per-minute charge.
- Ask whether your bill changes by location.
- Ask how the service handles sold-out items and tricky calls.

If you want a closer look at what should and should not be counted, read [what counts as a completed order](/blog/what-counts-as-completed-order).

sections.h2: How does AI phone answering cost compare with delivery apps and staff?
sections.body:
Many restaurants already know that delivery apps commonly take roughly **15% to 30% commission per order**. That is a very different cost structure from phone answering. If a $30 order goes through a delivery app, the commission can be far more than the phone-answering cost on the same order.

Human phone coverage is different again. Staff answering the phone can work well, but labor costs are usually paid whether the phone is ringing or not. Human answering services also usually bill per minute or per call, which can be hard to predict during dinner rush. For owners watching margins, it helps to compare the options side by side.

Use this rough comparison:
- **Delivery apps:** often take a percentage of the order.
- **Human answering services:** usually bill per minute or per call.
- **ROAL:** charges per completed phone order.

If your goal is to keep phone orders in-house and avoid app commission, compare the costs with [phone orders vs delivery apps](/compare/delivery-apps). If your issue is staffing, compare against [hiring phone staff](/compare/hiring-phone-staff).

sections.h2: What should I ask before I choose a phone answering tool?
sections.body:
Ask the questions that affect your bill and your service on a busy night. A cheap monthly price can still cost more if it adds per-minute charges, setup fees, or extra location fees. And a phone tool that cannot answer menu questions, quote ready times, or send clean tickets can create more work than it saves.

Use this owner checklist:
- What is the exact cost per completed order or per month?
- Are calls, questions, and test calls free?
- Is there a setup fee or contract?
- Can it take pickup and delivery orders from the live menu?
- Does it pass allergy-sensitive questions, complaints, and manager requests to staff?
- Does it send the ticket to the kitchen screen?

ROAL is built around those restaurant basics. The owner pastes a website, Google Maps link, or “Name, City” at /try, the host is built in about two minutes, and the owner can test-call it in the browser before going live. If you want to see the setup flow, [build a free test host](/try).

faq.q: How much does an AI phone answering service cost for a small restaurant?
faq.a: Many restaurant AI phone tools charge a monthly fee, often roughly $79 to $599 per location, even if order volume is low. ROAL charges $0.90 per completed phone order, with no monthly fee, setup fee, per-minute fee, or contract. That makes the cost easier to tie to actual orders.

faq.q: Is per-order pricing cheaper than a monthly plan?
faq.a: It depends on how many completed phone orders you get. Per-order pricing is often cheaper when volume is uneven or slower, while a monthly plan can be cheaper if you have very high order volume. The easiest way to compare is to multiply your monthly completed orders by $0.90 and compare that with the monthly fee.

faq.q: What counts as a completed order on the bill?
faq.a: A completed order is a confirmed order whose ticket reaches the kitchen screen. If the caller only asks questions, changes their mind, or the call does not become a confirmed order, it is not billed as a completed order. That definition keeps the cost tied to actual restaurant work.

faq.q: Can an AI phone host take payments over the phone?
faq.a: ROAL does not take card numbers over the phone. Payment happens at pickup or however the restaurant already takes it. It can take the order, name, phone number, ready time, and special notes, then send a clean ticket to the kitchen.
